purpose: Research record for the original bilingual BrowserHub guide on navigating lazy-loaded, infinite-scroll, virtualized and paginated browser content.

topicSelection.primaryIntent: Advance a browser agent through dynamic result lists without looping forever, skipping virtualized rows, misreading pagination, or claiming completeness without evidence.

existingOwners.ownedIntent: Output schemas, provenance, extraction coverage and returned-data completeness. It briefly recommends pagination coverage rules but does not teach bounded navigation through scroll, load-more, pagination and virtualized UI states.
Failure evidence and debugging traces. This new guide owns the navigation control loop and stopping decision, not general trace collection.

ownershipReview.distinctiveCoverage: Navigation rather than result schema: classify the list, locate the scroll owner, advance once, wait for a state change, collect IDs across recycled viewports, confirm page transitions, and state a bounded stop reason.

serpAndEditorialNotes.currentSearch: Search returned many general Playwright scrolling recipes and two relevant Stack Overflow questions. A separate root review identified several near-duplicate generic SEO recipes dated 2026-10-04, so the article avoids copying their recipe structure and adds an explicit bounded decision model, virtualized-list key capture, duplicate-click safeguards and honest completion reporting.

additionalPublicSignal.observation: A current search surfaced a user report that a listing appeared to contain 254 results while their browser script obtained 11–20 at a time. This is a user-reported example, not independently verified page behavior or a traffic metric; post date was not verified for this record.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright: Actions and scrolling
factsUsed: Playwright often scrolls elements into view automatically before actions.
The official guide gives scrolling an element into view as a way to trigger an infinite list.
For more precise scrolling, it documents mouse.wheel() and locator.evaluate() against a specific scrolling container.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright: Locator API
factsUsed: Locators re-resolve elements and support auto-waiting.
locator.all() returns the current matches immediately and may be unpredictable for a changing list.
Locator wait functions can wait for a custom observable condition.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright: Page API
factsUsed: page.waitForResponse() can match a URL or predicate and should be set before the triggering action.
Playwright discourages networkidle as a general readiness wait in tests; prefer observable web assertions or locator conditions.
waitForFunction() can wait for a page-specific condition.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright: Network
factsUsed: Network events and response waits can be used to observe page requests when a relevant endpoint is known.

claimsAndBoundaries: The sample code is a bounded template for an append-only list with inspected selectors; it was not run against a live site or fixture in this delegated task.
A fixed advance cap makes execution bounded; reaching the cap does not prove the list is complete.
Virtualized DOM row count is not a total. Preserve stable record IDs as viewports change and use explicit end or total signals where available.
Dynamic URLs can be poor deduplication keys; retain originals and normalize only understood parameters.
Playwright API names are scoped to Playwright and are not claimed as universal Browser Use, MCP or agent interfaces.
The guide does not recommend CAPTCHA, authentication, or access-control bypasses. It tells an agent to stop at those boundaries.
No paid search product or API was used. Firecrawl usage was not increased. No site was contacted by the sample code.
The sample was moved verbatim from the reviewed article draft into a downloadable .cjs asset. Only node --check was run; it was not executed against Chromium, a live URL, or a synthetic fixture.

sampleArtifact.purpose: Downloadable CommonJS bounded Playwright example. The bilingual article points to it because the article renderer does not support fenced code blocks or inline backtick formatting.
sampleArtifact.content: The full bounded sample previously reviewed: HTTP(S) URL validation before browser launch; finite 10-second action, 15-second navigation, and 8-second last-key waits; empty-card error; at most 40 scroll advances; end-marker-only complete status; try/finally cleanup; outer rejected-promise handler. The Playwright package is loaded with dynamic import inside the async entry point to satisfy the repository lint rule against require imports.
